characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded, rolling-direction-aligned discontinuous-precipitation microstructure; optical micrographs with 400 μm scale bars show fine, closely spaced lamellae (narrow inter-lamellar spacing) for the 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: analyse the microstructure of alloys at different processing conditions (hot-rolling and tempering)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM, 20 kV; magnifications X10,000 (1 µm scale bar); X2,500 available
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 9Al-10Mn-1C most of the austenite is transformed through the discontinuous precipitation reaction producing γ + κ-carbide fine lamellae; lamellar colonies fill most of the field with only a dark unreacted patch remaining.
characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (secondary electron imaging, SEI)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Table 3: EDS for Al and Mn in 9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C — Al wt% (Min/Mean/Max): δ 7.8/8.2/8.7, γ 7.6/7.8/8.0, K 8.0/8.2/8.3, γ nano-k 7.8/8.0/8.1; Mn wt%: δ 9.7/9.9/10.0, γ 9.9/10.3/10.7, k 10.2/10.4/10.5, γ nano-k 13.2/13.4/13.6. The nano-κ constituent is the Mn-richest phase; consistent with nano-sized κ-carbide in the non-transformed austenite. Analysis did not give clear/defined results but a reasonable interpretation was given with microscopy.
characterization_methods.purpose: provide qualitative information on the local phase composition and analyse phase chemistries
statistical analysis of hardening effects as a function of composition and process

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 9Al-10Mn-1C composition; temperature range 0–1300 °C; y-axis amount of all phases [mol] (0.00–1.10); phases FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21.
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic calculation (equilibrium phase volume fraction / amount of all phases vs temperature)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used qualitatively to explain the thermodynamic gradient in austenite stability between hot-rolling (1150 °C) and tempering (600 °C/800 °C); the γ fraction gradient was detected for 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C and 800 °C, consistent with the observed austenite decompositions.

interfaces.interface_notes: Interfaces involved are the γ/κ lamellar interphase boundaries produced by discontinuous precipitation and the δ/γ boundaries (δ phase possibly present). EDS (Table 3) partitions Al (δ 7.8–8.7, γ 7.6–8.0, K 8.0–8.3, γ nano-k 7.8–8.1 wt%) and Mn (δ 9.7–10.0, γ 9.9–10.7, k 10.2–10.5, γ nano-k 13.2–13.6 wt%) across δ, γ, κ and nano-κ constituents in this 600 °C tempered alloy.
interfaces.phase_evolution: γ → γ + κ discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C: a lower driving force caused by the lower annealing temperature (600 °C) allowed grain-boundary migration of the forming lamellar phase rather than completing lamellae separation; intergranular κ-carbides form on γ/γ boundaries. The residual austenite is present as band-shaped regions among the γ + κ lamellae, indicating a non-complete reaction.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Vickers hardness: 600 °C tempered 439 HV vs hot-rolled 273 HV

processing_steps.method: casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Resulted in 0.5 kg ingots (Table 1). Shared upstream step for the hot-rolled + quenched product that is subsequently tempered.
Parent process (proc_hot-rolled-1150c): ingots hot-rolled at 1150 °C obtaining 5 mm flat-products.
Hot-rolled product was water quenched before tempering.
Tempering at 600 °C for 30 min; triggers slight/incipient transformations — discontinuous precipitation and precipitation transformation.
Tempering at 600 °C for 30 min followed by water quenching.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers method; 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample for statistical analysis

phases_present.morphology: band-shaped regions surviving the transformation; light grey matrix in Fig. 1(b)
phases_present.texture: elongated bands aligned to rolling direction

phases_present.morphology: fine lamellae (discontinuous precipitation product, γ + κ lamellae)
phases_present.texture: lamellar colonies with fans of parallel lamellae

precipitates.distribution: lamellar colonies nucleating from grain boundaries; fill most of the field of view with fans of parallel lamellae impinging at colony boundaries
within the non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite (γ nano-k constituent detected by EDS, Table 3)

structures.overall_structure: Discontinuous (and precipitation) transformation of austenite: the microstructure is a banded, rolling-direction-aligned structure in which almost all of the austenite volume transformed into γ + κ-carbide fine lamellar colonies (discontinuous precipitation), with only a few band-shaped γ austenite regions surviving; some δ-phase may also be present. The non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite featured nano-sized κ-carbide precipitation. Dark transformed matrix is crossed by many bright white elongated bands/stringers.

unmapped_findings: Tempering at 600 °C triggered only slight/incipient transformations (discontinuous precipitation and precipitation transformation) in the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy, in contrast to 800 °C which triggered complete and widespread transformations (cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition). (b0117)

For 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C the tempering established thermodynamic changes for austenite stability; the manganese (10%) and carbon (1%) concentrations were not high enough to stabilize the γ phase against its own transformation, with the thermal energy introduced at 600 °C and the limited driving force permitting grain-boundary migration of the forming lamellar phase rather than completing lamellae separation. (b0062, b0067, b0068, b0069, b0070, b0071)

Discontinuous precipitation produced γ + κ-carbide fine lamellae in 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C; the best microstructure among the studied alloys is reported to be this 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C, with narrow inter-lamellar spacing, giving the highest hardness value (439 HV) and, per the literature, the better tensile ductility. (b0114, b0118)
The 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C gained outstanding hardness among the alloys featuring 9% aluminium, attributed to the fine γ + κ lamellae with short inter-lamellar spacing. (b0049, b0082, b0108)

EDS on the 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C indicated that the non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite contained nano-sized κ-carbide precipitation; the analysis did not give clear and defined results but a reasonable interpretation was given in accordance with the related microscopy observations. (b0034)
